subject: Adversarial fact-check of C:/Users/gurra/NeuroSem/docs/m0_evidence/tools/pyneuroml-jneuroml.research.json (pyNeuroML 1.3.22 + bundled jNeuroML 0.14.0)
verifier_environment: Windows 11 Home 10.0.22631, Git Bash, Python 3.12.10; fresh venv at C:/Users/gurra/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-gurra-Continuum/d876c622-d308-4d4a-bbf3-2b2374480647/scratchpad/m0/verify-pyneuroml-jneuroml/venv (pip install pyneuroml, unpinned, resolved 1.3.22); no Java on PATH; GitHub REST API via authenticated gh CLI and curl; raw source via raw.githubusercontent.com
overall_verdict: Most version, date, license, signature and behaviour claims were independently reproduced. Corrections: (1) pyNeuroML 'master' is a stale branch (setup.cfg version 1.3.8, JNEUROML_VERSION 0.13.3), and releases come from 'development', so the report's 'master activity after 1.3.22' framing and its 'unchanged on master' check are misleading. (2) LEMSSimulation has a 'meta' argument (documented for NEURON CVODE), so 'no integration-method parameter' is only narrowly true. (3) Current jLEMS / org.neuroml.export source points to jnml running flattened models with RK4 by default (Euler only for the non-flattened tree), which weakens the report's forward-Euler caveat. (4) The jNeuroML CI matrix exclusions are no-ops, and CI builds from source rather than the release jar. (5) On Windows, return_string=True returned an empty string when Java was missing, so the report's advice to use captured output for error classification does not work there. (6) jNeuroML's own Java main splits -I on ':', which strengthens the report's Windows include-path concern. No claim was found to be fabricated.

checks.verified_value: Current source contradicts using Euler as the working assumption for jnml. The bundled jar contains org.lemsml:jlems 0.12.0 (pom.properties), matching jLEMS 'development' pom 0.12.0 (no v0.12.0 tag exists). In that source: RUN.method = RK4 by default; Sim.run() calls run(true) (flatten), and runTree() uses the unflattened tree; StateInstance uses rk4Advance only when the state type is flattened and method is RK4, else eulerAdvance; a Meta 'method' attribute of rk4 or eulertree on the simulation control component overrides this. org.neuroml.export Utils.loadLemsFile (master and development) calls sim.run(). So jnml runs appear to use flattened RK4 where flattening succeeds, falling back to Euler otherwise. Not executed, and the bundled org.neuroml.export 1.11.0 has no matching git tag, so this is source-level evidence only

jNeuroML JNeuroML.java (v0.14.0) splits the -I / search-path argument on ':' (search.split(":")). Windows absolute include paths (C:\...) are therefore split at the drive letter inside Java, independent of pyNeuroML's quoting. Use relative include paths or run on Linux. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuroML/jNeuroML/v0.14.0/src/main/java/org/neuroml/JNeuroML.java

On Windows, pyneuroml.runners.execute_command_in_dir calls subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True) without stderr=STDOUT (Linux merges stderr). jnml error text is not captured into return_string output on Windows; the probe got (False, '') with Java missing. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML/v1.3.22/pyneuroml/runners.py

Java defaults for memory are bound at import time: pyneuroml/__init__.py reads JNML_MAX_MEMORY_LOCAL once, and function signatures embed '400M'. Set the env var before importing pyneuroml, or pass max_memory explicitly. jnml.bat (standalone jNeuroML 0.14.0) hard-codes -Xmx400M, ignores JNML_MAX_MEMORY_LOCAL and forwards only 6 arguments (%1..%6). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML/v1.3.22/pyneuroml/__init__.py ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuroML/jNeuroML/v0.14.0/jnml.bat

pyneuroml.io.write_neuroml2_file defaults to validate=True, which calls the jnml-backed validate_neuroml2. Mutation operators that write files will invoke Java (or silently get False without it) unless validate=False is passed. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML/v1.3.22/pyneuroml/io.py

libNeuroML is_valid_neuroml2 raises Exception('Not a valid NeuroML 2 doc ...') on malformed XML instead of returning False (empirical, truncated file). Its annotation is '-> None' although it returns bool. A NeuroSem pre-check must catch exceptions to classify 'structurally invalid'. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuralEnsemble/libNeuroML/v0.6.7/neuroml/utils.py

LEMSSimulation has a 'meta' argument documented for NEURON CVODE (method, abs_tolerance, rel_tolerance), and pynml exposes -cvode. This is relevant to the handoff's 'solver configuration' mutation family and to cross-simulator runs. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeuroML/pyNeuroML/v1.3.22/pyneuroml/lems/LEMSSimulation.py
